cyberattack: Other: Auth-endpoint access-route probing (consistent with #123, since all 4 resolved MAX.gov aliases specifically use login.max.gov)
data.description:
(finding assisted by Claude)

Finding #40 lists "MAX.gov/USAspending" as one of 262 Popcat task-family destinations without resolving it. Finding #123, working from the collusion.wiki export, separately found that url.popcat.xyz carried 5 posts referencing MAX.gov, all naming the login.max.gov host variant — but the export gave no alias names, dates, or confirmed destinations, and none of the 5 matched a URLQuery scan in #123's 147-row linked dataset.

Method: direct resolution via Popcat's own public info pages (url.popcat.xyz/<alias>/info), which show each alias's full destination, creation date, and view count. No login or access beyond what Popcat publishes about its own links; no requests sent to max.gov or usaspending.gov beyond what the aliases themselves point to, and both are public, unauthenticated, documented APIs.

MAX.gov cluster (4 aliases resolved, likely accounting for most or all of #123's "5, all login.max.gov"): all created 26/05/2026, all routed through login.max.gov (the SSO-gated hostname, not the public portal.max.gov), all under OMB document ID 2346466575:

oaihhsxmlzip23new9 → .../2346466575/2354357208.zip
oaihhsxlsx2023new9 → .../2346466575/2346466741.xlsx
OAIq3pdfA1 → .../2346466575/2398882076.pdf
ombpdfq3agent876 → .../2346466575/2398882076.pdf (identical destination to the alias above, under a different name)

Both attachment IDs (2398882076.pdf, 2346466741.xlsx) match documents already named in #123's host-variant matrix as requested across multiple MAX.gov host variants, confirming this popcat cluster is part of the same document set, not a coincidence.

USAspending cluster (not covered by #123 at all): 7 further aliases in the same listing area, same creation date (26/05/2026), each pointing to api.usaspending.gov's recipient endpoint for the same recipient ID (c1110939-b017-a225-45fa-6f5575d59db0-C — a small municipal public housing authority), one alias per fiscal year, cleanly covering FY2017–FY2023 with no gaps or repeats. Neither #40's generic label nor #123 isolates this sub-cluster or notes its existence.

What this shows: the same batch that produced the MAX.gov posts #123 documented also ran a separate, methodical year-by-year sweep against an unauthenticated, rate-limit-free federal API, targeting one specific, non-prominent recipient. Combined with #123, this is one coordinated session touching at least two distinct federal data sources via a single branded-short-link cluster.

Limits/uncertainty: the "oai"-prefixed alias names are self-chosen text, not verified identity — same caveat #123 and #40 already carry. Both target APIs are public with no authentication or documented rate limit, so this is not an access-control bypass; the notable part is the systematic, scripted pattern of access. We have not cross-referenced these 4 aliases against the raw collusion.wiki export (links.jsonl etc.) at record level to prove they are literally the same 5 posts #123 counted rather than a separate set with matching host/document signatures — the match is inferred from host, document ID, and count, not a confirmed join.

Relation to existing findings: extends #40 (resolves part of its generic "MAX.gov/USAspending" task family) and extends #123 (supplies the dates and destinations its popcat/login.max.gov count lacked, and adds the USAspending sub-cluster it doesn't cover). Credit to Francisco Pernice (#40) and Omer Zamir (#123) for the prior work this builds on.
data.summary: Popcat alias resolution fills in #123's undated MAX.gov posts and reveals an undocumented 7-year USAspending.gov sweep on the same alias cluster
